newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA AND WIBERG LINE UP FOR LAST CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA AND WIBERG LINE UP FOR LAST CHANCE.

text.p: Alberto Tomba and Pernilla Wiberg, last year's golden couple, each have one last chance on Saturday to take home a medal from the Alpine skiing world championships.
Both won two titles in Sierra Nevada, both have so far been disappointed this year.

Tomba, whose debut in Sestriere on Wednesday ended in disaster after just one minute, remains among the favourites for the floodlit night slalom, which is scheduled to close the championships, after he captured his first win of the season in Schladming two weeks ago.
But gamblers may be reluctant to bet on the flamboyant Italian's form, which has been questioned all winter after he was sidelined by illness and influenza.
Tomba insists he is still worth backing.

"I am very sorry but Saturday will be my day," Tomba told his disappointed but still devoted fans who are expected to show up in large numbers for what, in Italy at least, constitutes the showpiece event of the championships.
"It's true, I feel good in slalom. But I also felt good after my giant slalom training," he added. "I don't think that race will affect me in the slightest."
The triple Olympic and double world champion's recent record on the Kandahar piste has not been impressive.
The man who topped the slalom podium here in 1987, 1990, 1991, 1993 and 1994, failed to complete last year's World Cup race as well as an exhibition event on New Year's day.

He will face tough competition from the Austrians, who are hungry for a first gold after clinching six of the eight World Cup slaloms so far, with Thomas Sykora topping the podium five times and 1996 silver medallist Mario Reiter once.

Sykora has fully recovered from a hip injury sustained during a practice run before the Kitzbuehel slalom on January 26, and said: "I underwent a lot of therapy. I'm fine now and was able to train normally."
The Austrian remains calm although he has all the pressure from his ski-crazed nation on his shoulders.
"Of course I would prefer it if we already had a gold but I am fit and ready," he said.

Three Austrians swept the podium places in Sestriere last year with Reiter winning ahead of Sykora and 1994 Olympic champion Thomas Stangassinger -- who has finished second four times and third twice this season.
Slalom World Cup champion Sebastien Amiez is also a threat. The Frenchman has made four podium appearances this winter.
Wiberg, a triple world and double Olympic champion, faces a difficult task in the women's downhill earlier on Saturday.

Before the championships, the Swede who has at least one gold from every big event she has participated in, had her sights firmly set on the downhill title although she has never won a race in this discipline.
However, she thought differently after crashing out of the combined slalom on Thursday and failing to defend her combined gold, a week after being dethroned in slalom.
"It will be difficult to win the downhill," said Wiberg. "(Germany's Katja) Seizinger, (Swiss Heidi) Zurbriggen and (Italy's Isolde) Kostner were all very good in training."
She finished a poor super-G seventh and was sixth in the giant slalom which earned her a maiden gold in 1991.
Kostner will be bidding for another Italian gold following Deborah Compagnoni's wins in slalom and giant slalom and her own victory in the super-G on Tuesday.
Seizinger, the super-G silver medallist, has recovered from concussion sustained during a fall in Laax two weeks ago.
Saturday could also see the women's combined medals decided. The downhill section of the event was postponed on Thursday because of high winds and again on Friday after fresh snowfalls.
The race jury was considering on Friday how to rearrange the programme to fit in the combined downhill.
